title: Per-client rate limits need a distinguishable client — never pool unknown callers into one bucket
summary: A per-client limiter whose key falls back to a constant (no trusted peer IP) becomes a global cap that one anonymous caller can exhaust, locking everyone out.
reusable_steps: A per-client limiter whose key falls back to a constant (no trusted peer IP) becomes a global cap that one anonymous caller can exhaust, locking everyone out
expected_outcome: When a framework cannot supply a trustworthy peer address (e.g. Next.js 15+ has no request.ip and forwarded headers are spoofable without a trusted proxy), the per-client key degrades to a shared constant. A per-client cap on that key lets a single anonymous flood 429 every user. Apply only the whole-surface ceiling to indistinguishable callers, exempt proven loopback, evict least-recently-used buckets (not insertion-oldest) so key rotation cannot reset a hot client, and show a human-visible reason for any ignored state-changing GET such as a foreign /logout. Run the independent review before merge so such findings land in the same PR.
